title: F33: an inbox item must declare its fix surface when it is filed — a free-text-only surface cannot be routed
summary: F29 routes on the surface a record STATES (a pipeline-* kind, declared files[], or full repo paths its text names). Items that name protected files only by basename ("ship_recovery.go", "audit.go") or partial path ("phases/audit/audit.go:131") carry no typed surface, so they stay lane-eligible and die at triage when the LLM resolves the real path. On 2026-09-26 the queue's top-weighted item (resume-does-not-refresh-a-stale-worktree-base, 0.86) and two others were hand-typed by the console before wave 7.
fix: Fix the producer, not the classifier: `evolve inbox` gains a lint (and the console filing paths — the halt autofiler, retro/memo filers, operator templates — a check) that an item declares its surface: a pipeline-* kind, or files[] with at least one path-shaped token (inboxbatch.Item.DeclaredSurface). Report undeclared dispatchable items with the protected basenames their text names; never guess a path.
acceptance: `evolve inbox` reports every dispatchable item that declares no surface (no pipeline-* kind, no path-shaped files[] token — inboxbatch.Item.DeclaredSurface), naming the protected basenames its text names; it never guesses a path.
The console filing paths the repo owns (the ADR-0072 halt autofiler, the retro/memo filers) write files[] or a pipeline-* kind on every item they file; a test per filer pins it.

Replay: the three items hand-typed on 2026-09-26 (resume-does-not-refresh-a-stale-worktree-base, carryover-queue-unbounded-by-design, acs-verdict-filename-literal-sweep) are reported as undeclared on their pre-curation records.
